Each wing has 12 beds, with most rooms private, and serves as the hospital’s dedicated home for peritoneal dialysis patients (a specialty admitted only to our units). Supported by many tenured nurse preceptors, you’ll build strong core skills and a standout foundation for your next step, including travel nursing and specialty roles, while delivering an exceptional patient experience through clear communication, comfort, and dignity. Fluent is building the next generation advertising network: Partner Monetize and Advertiser Acquisition. Our vision is to build an ML/AI first network of advertisers and publishers working toward a common objective, elevating relevancy in e-commerce for everyday shoppers.
  
  
Fluent is hiring its first dedicated AI Engineer. Over the past year, AI at Fluent has moved from pilots to production: a service desk agent that closes tickets without a human touch, a pipeline that cut modeled audience delivery from days to hours, and an agent that audits cross-system attribution and identifies revenue reconciliation opportunities. All of it was built by people doing it alongside their day jobs. Your job is to make it your day job.
  
  
You will sit in Core Engineering and work every day with Data Engineering, Data Science, and Solution Architecture. You will build the agents and automated workflows our business teams have asked for, and you will build them on the Databricks lakehouse that is Fluent's data hub, because the hard part of most of these workflows is not the model. It is getting trusted data and reliable actions in front of it.
  
  
You are a builder who ships. You are strong in Python and SQL, you have put at least one LLM-powered application in front of real users, and you know the difference between a demo and a production system: evaluation, monitoring, cost, and a clear owner. You have worked in Databricks or a comparable lakehouse, or you have the data engineering depth to get productive there quickly. You are comfortable sitting with a support lead or an account manager, understanding how they actually work, and turning that into something that runs every day. This role is fully remote in the United States, with occasional travel to our New York headquarters.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Ship production agents and automated workflows from a prioritized, business-validated backlog. Own each one from scoping with the business owner through build, deployment, monitoring, documentation, and handoff.
* Build the data foundation those workflows depend on in Databricks: Unity Catalog tables and views, Lakeflow pipelines, Lakeflow Connect ingestion from systems like HubSpot, and Genie spaces that let business teams ask questions in plain language. Bring data from our ad-serving and partner platforms, CRM, support desk, and finance systems into one place people can trust.
* Work with Data Science to make agent quality measurable: evaluation sets, accuracy and drift tracking, cost and latency instrumentation, and the audit fields and failure alerts every production workflow carries.
* Integrate with Fluent's systems through APIs, webhooks, MCP servers, and orchestration (Databricks Workflows, n8n, GitHub Actions), and replace brittle point-to-point automations with maintained, observable ones.
* Partner with Core Engineering to expose platform data and actions as APIs, so agents and business teams can use them directly instead of routing requests through engineers.
* Build reusable pieces, not one-offs: Claude skills, MCP connectors, prompt and evaluation libraries, and playbooks that other builders across Fluent can pick up.
* Handle consumer data in line with Fluent's privacy and compliance standards, use only approved AI tools, and work with IT & Security on credentials and access.
* Demo weekly, write things down in Confluence, and share what you learn in brown bags and tech talks.
* Use AI-assisted development (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot review) as a normal part of how you work.

****What success looks like****
In your first 90 days you will have shipped one workflow end to end, with a named business owner and numbers Finance can validate. By six months you will have several in production, at least one reusable component another builder has picked up, and a clear view of what next quarter's backlog should be.
  
  
**Requirements**

* 3+ years of professional software or data engineering experience, with strong Python and SQL.
* You have built and shipped at least one LLM-powered application or agent that real users depend on, using tool calling, retrieval, structured outputs, and evaluation.
* Hands-on experience with Databricks (Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Workflows) or a comparable lakehouse, or deep enough data engineering experience to ramp quickly.
* Experience integrating SaaS and internal systems through REST APIs, webhooks, and OAuth.
* You test your work, instrument it, and care about cost. You know when a workflow is ready to be owned by someone else.
* You communicate clearly with people who do not write code, and you are comfortable running a working session with a business team.
* Experience using AI coding assistants (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) as part of a modern engineering workflow.
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

****Nice to have****

* Databricks Mosaic AI (Agent Framework, Model Serving, Vector Search), Genie, Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, Lakebase, or Databricks Apps.
* Building MCP servers, or working with the Claude Developer Platform or Agent SDK.
* Workflow orchestration tools such as n8n.
* Integrations with HubSpot, Zendesk, NetSuite, or Jira.
* Experience in ad tech, performance marketing, or another environment that handles regulated consumer data.

**Who are we?**
Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.
  
  
We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.
  
  
We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.
  
  
We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!
  
  
Why this team?
  
  
Internal Infrastructure builds the infrastructure and tools used to train, evaluate, and serve Cohere's foundation models. You will work with AI researchers and ML engineers on stability, scalability, and observability. The work accelerates the models behind Cohere's platform, North.
  
  
You will build the platform that runs training, evaluation, and reinforcement-learning workloads: job lifecycle, scheduling, workload networking, and the storage those jobs depend on. The role includes a compensated 24x7 on-call rotation.
  
  
What you will do
  
  

* Own the platform that schedules and runs training, evaluation, and reinforcement-learning jobs on Kubernetes: who gets capacity, what happens when a job fails, and how a researcher finds out whether the platform caused it.
* Build the networking and runtime isolation those workloads need, including agent and sandbox environments.
* Work with the data infrastructure team on storage for checkpoints and other training artifacts.
* Troubleshoot production failures and performance problems, and leave the system easier to operate than you found it.
* Build automation, infrastructure-as-code, and observability so the platform stays maintainable.

We hire at more than one level. We set level based on the scope you've owned and how independently you drive work.
  
  
You may be a good fit if you have
  
  

* Run a job platform, batch system, or Kubernetes controllers in production. Scheduling, queues, and multi-tenant fairness are central to this work.
* Shown distributed systems judgment: retries, partial failure, and knowing what not to automate.
* Worked on ML training workflows, RL sandboxes, container networking (CNI), or checkpoint storage at scale. Direct GPU-cluster experience is a plus.
* Written software in Python or Go. You would rather extend a solid open-source project than rebuild it.
* Worked with researchers, ML engineers, or another team whose goals were not identical to yours.
* Found a bottleneck, proposed a fix, and driven it in a fast-moving environment.

If this does not line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

Expedia Technology teams partner with our Product teams to create innovative products, services, and tools to deliver high-quality experiences for travelers, partners, and our employees. * Experience in the travel or e-commerce industry
* Publications in top-tier ML conferences or journals
* Patented Inventions, pending and issued
* Contributions to open-source ML projects
* Experience taking models from prototype to production in collaboration with Machine Learning Engineering teams

**Introduction To The Team**
Expedia Technology teams partner with our Product teams to create innovative products, services, and tools to deliver high-quality experiences for travelers, partners, and our employees. A singular technology platform powered by data and machine learning provides secure, differentiated, and personalized experiences that drive loyalty and traveler satisfaction.
  
  
The Traveler Discovery & Planning team at Expedia is at the forefront of innovation in AI-driven agentic systems. We're dedicated to enhancing customer experiences, increasing engagement, and strengthening traveler relationships through cutting-edge machine learning solutions. Our work directly impacts millions of travelers worldwide, shaping their journey from dreaming to booking and beyond.
  
  
Join a team that’s focused on Agentic Experiences revolutionizing traveler experiences through autonomous, intelligent agent systems. **In This Role, You Will**

* Design, build, and evaluate multi-step agentic AI systems, including autonomous agents capable of planning, tool use, memory management, and multi-agent collaboration
* Research and implement state-of-the-art techniques in agentic architectures, such as ReAct, reflection loops, chain-of-thought prompting, and tool-augmented reasoning

* Experience integrating LLMs with external tools, APIs, and structured data sources for real-world task completion
* Understanding of prompt engineering techniques including chain-of-thought, few-shot prompting, and structured output generation
* Experience defining and running evaluation frameworks for ML systems, including offline benchmarking and production monitoring

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Publications in top-tier ML conferences or journals

**About The Team**
Across industries, OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering (AIE) team helps organizations turn frontier AI into safe, reliable production systems that deliver meaningful business outcomes. We work directly with customers’ engineering, product, security, and transformation teams to navigate complex architectures, data environments, governance requirements, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better OpenAI products and reusable patterns that help customers move faster.
  
  
**About The Role**
As an Enterprise AIE, you will serve as a technical partner to leading organizations within the Healthcare and Life Sciences segment (HLS), helping them turn ambitious AI use cases into durable production systems and adoption at scale. You will combine deep technical judgment with hands-on engineering to provide technical leadership on complex customer deployments. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions about model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. You will work across clinical, operational, administrative and research workflows, translating security, privacy and governance requirements into practical deployment decisions. Success is measured by durable production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful business impact. Your deployment experience will also directly influence how OpenAI’s products evolve.
  
  
This role may be based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco, or it may be performed remotely. Office-based employees follow a hybrid work model with three days per week in the office. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.
  
  
**In This Role, You Will**

* Work hands-on in code to design, build, evaluate, and deploy AI systems from prototype to reliable production and scaled adoption that solve important customer problems and deliver measurable business outcomes.
* Partner with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and success criteria.
* Make sound technical decisions across model selection, agent and tool design, retrieval, context design, data pipelines, evaluation, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.
* Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers to resolution.
* Partner closely with customers’ engineering teams and OpenAI’s Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Go-to-Market teams to turn deployment experience into actionable product feedback.
* Partner with customer security, privacy, clinical and business teams to design responsible AI deployments, including data handling, access controls, evaluation, human oversight and monitoring.
* Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

**You Might Thrive in This Role If You**

* Have personally designed, built, and shipped AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, taking them from prototype to production and making substantial contributions through coding, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.
* Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working end to end across model APIs, agent and tool development, retrieval and data pipelines, evaluation, observability, integrations, and production operations. Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.
* Know how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, automated graders, production signals, and human judgment.
* Have navigated enterprise production requirements, including integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.
* Have experience delivering AI or software in healthcare, life sciences or similarly complex regulated enterprises, with measurable outcomes beyond a proof of concept and familiarity with sensitive data, legacy systems and interoperability.
* Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
* Communicate clearly and credibly with hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security and product teams, and executives.
* Take end-to-end ownership, exercise strong technical judgment, and move effectively through ambiguity.

**Position Purpose**
The Research Software Engineer at the
**Center for Open Neuroscience ( CON )**
helps build infrastructure that makes neuroscience data FAIR , open, and reproducible, working on open-source projects such as DataLad, DANDI , EMBER , and OpenNeuro Archives. Essential duties include designing and implementing workflows for versioned data management and processing, applying them to real data wrangling tasks, contributing to national neuroimaging data archives, and helping shape the standards for how neuroscience data is organized and shared. The role involves collaborating with developers, neuroscientists, and standards architects across institutions and countries.
  
  
****Description****
The
**CON**
, part of the Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences at Dartmouth College, is seeking a Neuroinformagician — an enthusiastic Research Software Engineer to help build the infrastructure that makes neuroscience FAIR , Open, and Reproducible at scale. You will work on and with flagship open-source projects -including DataLad, ReproNim, DANDI , EMBER , and OpenNeuro Archives, and others – that are used by thousands of researchers worldwide and are central to the NIH BRAIN Initiative’s ecosystem.
  
  
This is a high-impact role at the intersection of scientific computing, data engineering, and open-source community building. You will design and implement workflows for versioned data management and processing, apply them to real data wrangling tasks, contribute to national neuroimaging data archives, and help shape the standards that define how neuroscience data is organized and shared. Your work will directly accelerate brain research across hundreds of laboratories.
  
  
You will collaborate with a diverse network of developers, neuroscientists, and standards architects across institutions and countries. The role offers genuine opportunities for professional growth — whether that means deepening expertise in distributed systems, learning neuroscience domain knowledge, contributing to published research, or developing leadership within open-source communities. Opportunities to present work and engage with collaborators at scientific conferences and developer sprints are available for those who enjoy them and have content to deliver!

**Code Development and Maintenance:**
Design, implement, and maintain open-source software and standards for large-scale scientific data versioning, distribution, and archiving. This includes contributing to core tools (DataLad and git-annex ecosystem, DANDI CLI / API ), building and improving pipelines for ingesting and validating datasets against community standards ( BIDS , NWB , HED ), and developing containerized and cloud-native solutions for data processing and delivery. 25%

15%

**ABOUT THE POSITION**

Groundswell builds community power - cutting electricity bills for the neighbors who need savings most through community solar, resilience hubs, and home energy efficiency and repair. Gratava is the AI-enabled data platform underneath that work: a neutral coordination layer where a household proves eligibility once and that verified record unlocks every program they qualify for.

Forward deployed means living with our users, customers, and partners. The Forward Deployed Engineer will sit with utility staff, program administrators, caseworkers and households to find what blocks or limits adoption and success - then build the prototypes that prove the solution works, validate it with the customer, and hand it off to production engineering. Customer contact and building are one job here.

Reporting to the SVP, Data Platform, the Forward Deployed Engineer is a peer to the Tech Lead with distinct ownership: the Forward Deployed Engineer proves what should be built, and the Tech Lead is responsible for what ships in production. You will write production-quality code, and what you build is judged by whether it proves the answer rather than by whether it ships - deployment into production, and the policies and controls that go with it, stay with the Tech Lead.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

•
**Field discovery**
. Work directly with our internal teams and with utilities, program administrators, agencies and households to understand where systems, policies, and data break down in practice. You will investigate hard problems such as premise resolution, income verification, eligibility determination, program matching, and other rules that have not yet been defined.

•
**Build the proof.**
Turn ambiguous problems into working software. Build new core functionality at the prototype level - the matching engine, the rules-as-logic layer, the AI agent layer - connected to real data sources and run against real records. Be responsible for both demonstrating an idea and building enough of it to prove whether it works and adds value. Prototype here means scope, not craft - you write code good enough to run in production, even though production deployment is determined by the Tech Lead.

•
**Program rules into working logic**
. Translate complex heterogeneous program

requirements into reliable, testable logic such as income thresholds, categorical

eligibility, funding stack sequencing, pre-weatherization gating and other program

specific conditions in ways that are explainable, auditable, and resilient.

•
**Validate with the customer.**
Responsible for building prototypes and testing with

the people who will use them. Before production engineering begins, establish

three things: the data sources work as expected; the logic produces the correct

outcomes, and the interface is simple enough for customers to understand and

use.

•
**Create a clean path to production**
. Deliver a working proof, the data connections,

technical decisions behind it, and a clear specification that distinguishes what is

essential from what is not. Give production engineering enough clarity to complete

the work without having to discover the problem.

•
**Scope the roadmap**
. Turn technical discovery into actionable products and

engineering decisions. Provide fast, reliable feasibility assessments and effort

estimates that leadership and engineering can use to make and commit to

roadmap decisions.

•
**Continual Development and Growth**
. Share what you know and learn with the

broader engineering team. Partner closely with the Tech Lead to transfer agentic

tooling practice and document knowledge that compounds across the team.

We’re looking for a Software Engineer, Billing to build the systems that make Braintrust’s pricing, usage, and payments accurate, scalable, and transparent.

**Job Description**
The Role
  
  
The R&D Manufacturing Systems Research Group at General Motors is seeking a researcher to develop and apply artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions for advanced manufacturing systems.
  
  
This role will focus on applying AI/ML to real-world manufacturing challenges involving process improvement, quality, automation, production efficiency, and decision support. The researcher will work with multidisciplinary teams to develop new concepts, build prototypes, evaluate results, and help transition successful solutions into manufacturing applications.
  
  
What You Will Do
  
  
You will conduct applied research and technical development at the intersection of AI/ML and manufacturing systems. You will collaborate with researchers, manufacturing engineers, plant personnel, operational teams, and external partners to identify opportunities and develop practical solutions.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  

* Develop and evaluate AI/ML models for manufacturing engineering and production applications.
* Build data pipelines, prototypes, analytical tools, and decision-support solutions.
* Apply methods including machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, large language models, computer vision, time-series modeling, and optimization.
* Work with manufacturing data from sensors, equipment, processes, simulations, and operational systems.
* Translate engineering and manufacturing challenges into research questions and technical plans.
* Design experiments, validate results, and assess technical and business impact.
* Evaluate emerging AI/ML technologies and determine their potential value for GM manufacturing systems.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams, universities, suppliers, and technical experts.
* Communicate technical results through presentations, reports, publications, and invention disclosures.
* Maintain current knowledge of AI/ML methods, tools, and responsible AI practices.

**Required Qualifications**

* Master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related field.
* Experience developing and evaluating AI/ML models through academic research, industrial research, internships, or applied engineering projects.
* Proficiency in Python and experience with AI/ML frameworks or analytical tools.
* Knowledge of data preparation, model training, validation, performance evaluation, and experiment design.
* Experience working with structured or unstructured data, such as sensor, time-series, image, text, or process data.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.
* Ability to work independently and contribute effectively to a multidisciplinary research team.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience applying AI/ML to manufacturing, engineering, robotics, automation, scientific computing, or industrial operations.
* Knowledge of manufacturing process modeling, process control, quality systems, production systems, optimization, or operations research.
* Experience with computer vision, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, digital twins, simulation, reinforcement learning, generative AI, large language models, or agentic systems.
* Experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Keras, MATLAB, R, SQL, or cloud-based AI/ML platforms.
* Experience designing data architectures, integrating databases, or deploying models into operational environments.
* Familiarity with MLOps, model monitoring, model lifecycle management, and responsible AI.
* Peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, patents, or invention disclosures.
* Experience collaborating with universities, suppliers, research institutions, or distributed technical teams.

**About The Company**
Braintrust is the agent observability platform. By actively applying intelligence to agent traces and automatically surfacing the most critical patterns, Braintrust gives teams the visibility to understand how agents behave in production and the tools to improve them.
  
  
Teams at Notion, Stripe, Box, OpenAI, and Cloudflare use Braintrust to trace their agents, find the issues in their observability data, and run evals that tell them how to improve.
  
  
**About The Role**
We’re looking for a Software Engineer, Billing to build the systems that make Braintrust’s pricing, usage, and payments accurate, scalable, and transparent.
  
  
Braintrust helps teams observe, evaluate, and improve production AI agents. Our customers generate large volumes of traces, run automated and human evaluations, use AI-powered product features, and retain data under different plans and policies. Billing needs to turn those product activities into clear, reliable customer experiences—from usage measurement and plan enforcement to invoices, credits, and account state.
  
  
You’ll work across the billing stack: usage metering, subscriptions and entitlements, payment integrations, invoicing, credits, and the internal systems that reconcile them. This is a deeply technical IC role. It is not a finance-operations role, and it is not a backend generalist role that contributes to billing occasionally.
  
  
You’ll be a technical authority on billing correctness and scale, helping Braintrust launch pricing models that let customers adopt the platform with confidence as their AI workloads grow.
  
  
**What You'll Do**
Core responsibilities:
  
  

* Own Braintrust billing architecture end-to-end, including metering, plans, subscriptions, entitlements, invoices, credits and payments.
* Design our billing architecture to solve immediate needs and simplify billing for new features as they are developed and released.
* Ensure Braintrust accurately measures and bills for product usage, including processed data, evaluation scores, model usage, and data retention.
* Partner with product, infrastructure, finance, and customer-facing teams to introduce new pricing models and billing workflows with confidence.

Build the systems that power Braintrust billing, such as:
  
  

* A reliable usage-metering and aggregation pipeline that turns product activity into accurate customer usage.
* A subscription, limits, and entitlement system that supports plan allowances, feature access, trials, upgrades, and on-demand usage.
* Internal tools and APIs for investigating billing anomalies, issuing credits, and helping customers understand their account state.
* Observability across the billing pipeline, including metering lag, event completeness, reconciliation discrepancies, and payment health.

**Ideal candidate credentials**

* Expert-level understanding of TypeScript, Rust, SQL, backend systems, APIs, and distributed data-processing patterns
* Experience building and operating production usage-based billing, payments, or subscription systems
* Experience with metering, aggregation, idempotency, reconciliation, and event-driven architectures
* Experience integrating with Stripe or similar payment infrastructure
* Experience building or maintaining financial ledgers, credits, balances, or invoice systems is a plus
* Comfortable shipping end-to-end, from backend infrastructure and data systems to internal tools and customer-facing UI
* Previous experience founding or working at startups is a plus
* Has an appreciation for the tension between moving quickly and preserving customer trust and billing correctness

Benefits include
  
  

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Daily lunch, snacks, and beverages
* Flexible time off
* Competitive salary and equity
* Wifi & cellphone stipend

Equal opportunity

**Description**
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.
  
  
The Team Join the next science revolution at AWS Life Sciences Applied AI Solutions where you'll work alongside world-class scientists to build AI that transforms how therapeutics are discovered, developed, and brought to patients.
  
  
We're out to revolutionize how medicines are discovered, developed, and brought to patients powered by a new generation of AI. Our team tackles some of the hardest open problems at the intersection of frontier AI and life sciences. We apply biological foundation models large language models and agentic reasoning systems to life sciences problems then put them into the hands of customers as applications and managed services they can fine-tune tailor and deploy on their own data. The science challenges are deep: how do you design agentic systems that reason correctly over complex biological regulatory and clinical logic? How do you enable customers to tailor foundation models to their proprietary data and get better outputs with less effort? How do you adapt models to reason faithfully in high-stakes scientific and regulatory domains?
  
  
Today we're focused on two areas. In clinical trials we're building AI that automates and optimizes regulatory and clinical development workflows. In drug design our products (including Amazon Bio Discovery) accelerate discovery by giving bench scientists AI-guided protein engineering and antibody design capabilities. We combine frontier research with production-scale delivery to put breakthrough science into the hands of customers solving humanity's hardest problems.
